value.body: Runs routine tests and keeps lab equipment ready in colleges, research institutes and industrial labs. Lab technicians prepare samples, solutions and apparatus, maintain and calibrate instruments, manage stock and assist scientists, faculty or students. The work follows set procedures and safety rules.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc in Physics, Chemistry or Life Sciences
items.note: Medical lab roles need a DMLT or B.Sc MLT instead

items.label: Where the work is
items.value: Colleges, universities, research institutes, industrial and testing labs

items.label: Government posts
items.value: Filled through institute notifications and recruitment commissions

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers apply to lab assistant or technician posts advertised by colleges, universities, research institutes and private labs. Government institutions recruit through published notifications and written or skill tests. Practical lab experience from the degree, and comfort with instruments and record-keeping, carry the most weight.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is steady and procedure-driven; the scope depends heavily on the lab.
Next steps: senior technician, lab in-charge, or a research assistant role after an M.Sc.
Clinical or medical lab work needs specific MLT qualifications, separate from a general B.Sc.
